msg: THE BOUND THIS BENCH EXISTS FOR, and the failure mode blocks.md s7 item 5 names by name - 'a habitual 1 uF fitted outside the reference's stability window'. Total VREF bypass C5 + C3 in uF, gated against the ADR4520's LOAD CAPACITANCE spec, which is a TWO-ENDED MANDATORY window: 1 uF MIN and 100 uF MAX [Table 3 p.3, C579305.json layout_notes[4] and decoupling[VOUT]; Table 12 'Minimum COUT Value' cross-confirms 1.0 uF for this member; Applications Information p.31 'An output capacitor is required for stability']. The output capacitor is a compensation element inside the reference's own loop, so EXCEEDING 100 uF is as out-of-spec as going under 1 uF - which is the half a one-ended reading misses. Measured 49.2 uF: 49x above the floor, 2x below the ceiling, so no X7R tolerance or DC-bias derating can walk it out from either end. SEEDED DEFECTS: bulk value-engineered down to a habitual 100 nF reads 0.1 and trips the floor; C3 raised to 150 uF because 'more bulk must be safer' reads 152.2 and trips the ceiling while every other measure in this deck IMPROVES.

THE LITERAL PROMISE of blocks.md s7 item 5: VREF back within 15.6 uV of its settled value before the next conversion begins. Measured cycle-to-cycle at 22.7 kSa/s - t_CYC = 22 DCLOCKs = 44.0 us at the 500 kHz DCLOCK, the FASTEST this board can run and so the least recovery time it can ever have (C544731.json abs_max 112). Measured 0.0014 uV. The reference is in periodic steady state by this point in the run, which is what this number confirms; it goes to 6.8 uV if the reference's output impedance is pushed to an implausible 50 ohm.

peak-to-peak VREF excursion inside one steady-state conversion cycle - the quantity a conversion running in repetitive operation actually sees, and the one that maps to a code error (a CONSTANT VREF offset is a gain term the error budget already carries in s5 rows 4-6; only the variation is new). Measured 4.75 uV = 0.30 LSB-halves. Because rref*Cbulk = 246 us is much longer than t_CYC = 44 us, VREF never returns to quiescent between conversions: it settles to a cycle-average sag with a small ripple on top, and the ripple is SMALLER than the single-shot droop, not larger. Trips at 134 uV when the bulk is cut to 100 nF.

FINDING, EXPECTED TO FIRE, AND HANDED TO THE ARCHITECT. VREF droop across the FIRST conversion after an idle period - the one case where the node starts fully recovered, so the whole per-conversion charge comes out of the bulk. Measured 16.35 uV against blocks.md s7 item 5's 15.6 uV figure: 1.05x over, i.e. 1.05 LSB-halves. It is a WARNING and not an error because s7 item 5 states its 15.6 uV as a RECOVERY criterion (ref_recov_uv, which passes at 0.0014 uV), and intra-conversion droop is a different quantity that no cited source bounds on this board. Three things the architect needs with it: (1) it applies to the first conversion after idle only - repetitive operation sees 4.75 uV; (2) the droop is monotonic across the bit trials, so the code error is a fraction of the raw droop (the MSB decisions happen before the droop develops) - that fraction is NOT quantified here; (3) the remedy is bounded, because more bulk is the only lever and the ADR4520 ceiling is 100 uF total, so the best available is 49.2 -> ~100 uF, which halves it to ~8.5 uV. Not sensitive to the unpublished reference output impedance: 16.35 uV at 5 ohm, 17.33 uV at 50 ohm, saturating at droop_caplimit_uv.

the ESTIMATE-FREE upper bound on any single-conversion droop: Qdyn / Cbulk, the limit in which the reference contributes nothing and the bulk supplies every coulomb. 0.858 nC / 49.2 uF = 17.44 uV. Qdyn is DERIVED, not guessed, from the ADS8326's two published reference-current rows - 14 uA MAX at 10 kHz and 220 uA MAX at 250 kHz [C544731.json abs_max 84/83] - solved as I(f) = Istatic + Qdyn*f, giving Qdyn = 0.858 nC per conversion and Istatic = 5.42 uA. (The 14 uA row also CORRECTS constraints.json, which records 7 uA - the error state.json decision 76 flags.) This bound carries no rref and no solver in it: it is arithmetic on two datasheet rows and two fitted capacitor values, and it is what makes the whole bench robust to the reference model. Reads 8580 uV when the bulk is cut to 100 nF.

the same closed-form limit on the PESSIMISTIC reading of the reference-current split, in which the entire 14 uA / 10 kHz row is charged to dynamic redistribution rather than being split with a static component: 1.4 nC / 49.2 uF = 28.5 uV. Carried so the two-row fit behind droop_caplimit_uv is visible as a modelling choice rather than a hidden one, and so a reader who rejects that fit still has their number. Ceiling 40 uV keeps it live against a bulk reduction without asserting 28.5 uV as a promise.

steady DC sag of VREF below quiescent under the SAR's average reference load (Istatic 5.42 uA plus the burst average), through the modelled reference output impedance. Measured 95.1 uV = 46 ppm of 2.048 V. This is a GAIN term, not a settling term - blocks.md s5 rows 4/5/6 carry the reference's DC error budget - and it is reported for scale and because it is the one number in this deck that IS proportional to the unpublished rref (7.2 uV at 0.5 ohm, 589 uV at 50 ohm), so it flags if that boundary value is ever changed. It is NOT a design promise and no cited source bounds it.
